summary.intent: Execute Phase 19.2 gap closure plans to fix two verification failures: missing PERF-09 requirement definition and non-definitive post-optimization baselines due to mismatched test environments.
summary.outcome: PERF-09 was registered in REQUIREMENTS.md and a replanned three-point local baseline approach was adopted (replacing a destructive staging deployment). Gap closure plans 03 and 04 were spawned for execution, with 19.2-04 redesigned to collect matched-environment baselines across three optimization stages.

repo: Phase 19.2 covers IPFS upload performance optimization — primary bottleneck was sequential IPNS publish + folder metadata update, fixed via Promise.allSettled concurrent execution
Kubo is configured via Docker Compose with IPFS_PROFILE=server,pebbleds; switching datastores requires volume deletion (destructive)
Load test harness at tests/load/src/ uses a scenario/harness architecture — upload-throughput scenario runs N clients × 20 files (1KB-500KB) capturing p50/p95/p99/min/max/avg and throughput ops/s
Pre/post baselines are stored in .planning/baselines/ as markdown files
REQUIREMENTS.md had a PERF-09 gap — both plans referenced it but it was never defined; requirements only went to PERF-08
Git commits for phase 19.2 include distinct checkpoints for baseline capture, SDK changes, and infrastructure changes — usable as checkout points for isolated benchmarking

code.finding: Upload throughput scenario — N clients × 20 files each with sizes 1KB-500KB
Collects per-operation p50/p95/p99/min/max/avg latencies plus throughput ops/s
Manages concurrent test clients for load scenarios

workflow: Verification failures with mismatched test environments (staging vs localhost, different client counts) produce non-definitive results — always use matched-condition baselines
Three-point isolated benchmarking (no opts / SDK only / SDK+infra) gives cleaner signal than single before/after comparison
Gap closure plans should be numbered sequentially after completed plans (01, 02 done → gaps start at 03)
Pushing a feature branch to remote before requiring infrastructure changes on a remote host is an efficient handoff pattern

friction: Original post-optimization baselines were captured in different environments (staging vs localhost) with different client counts (10 vs 5), making verification non-definitive — required replanning
Switching from flatfs to pebbleds datastore requires deleting the IPFS Docker volume, which wipes all pinned content — destructive operation that blocked the original staging validation approach
PERF-09 was referenced in both completed plans but never formally defined in REQUIREMENTS.md — a planning oversight that only surfaced at verification
